etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle French flexible, from Latin flexibilis, from flectō (“I bend, curve”).

Morphologically flex +‎ -ible.

definitions.definition: Capable of being flexed or bent without breaking; able to be turned or twisted without breaking.

quote.citation: c. 1602, William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Troylus and Cressida”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act I, scene iii]:
quote.text: When the splitting wind Makes flexible the knees of knotted oaks.

definitions.definition: Willing or prone to give way to the influence of others; not invincibly rigid or obstinate.

quote.citation: 1625, Francis [Bacon], “(please specify the chapter)”, in The Essayes […], 3rd edition, London:  […]  Iohn Haviland for Hanna Barret, →OCLC:
quote.text: Phocion the Athenian (a man of great severity, and no ways flexible to the will of the people […]

quote.citation: c. 1591–1592 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Third Part of Henry the Sixt, […]”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act I, scene iv]:
quote.text: Women are soft, mild, pitiful, and flexible.

definitions.definition: Capable of adapting or changing to suit new or modified conditions or situations.

You can't always get what you want: you need to learn to be flexible.

definitions.definition: Capable or being adapted or molded in some way.

quote.citation: 1735, John Rogers, Nineteen Sermons on various occasions:
quote.text: This they foresaw was a Principle more flexible to their Purpose

definitions.definition: (chiefly engineering and manufacturing) Something that is flexible.

quote.citation: 2009 August 19, Terry McCrann, “Win-win deal for the times”, in Herald Sun‎[1], archived from the original on 22 August 2009:
quote.text: Alcan is mostly flexibles -- and so it boosts Amcor's flexible packaging business to a globally significant $7 billion one.
